mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI engine costs £2,200-£4,500 supply-only, or £3,000-£6,000 fully fitted depending on the generation (B8 EA189 vs B9 EA288) and supplier location. Used engines start around £900 but carry higher risk for emissions components. B8 EA189 (CAGA/CFFB): £2,200-£3,800 reconditioned. B9 EA288 (CNHA/DEUA): £2,800-£4,500 reconditioned. Supply & fit labour typically adds £600-£900.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 2.0 TDI and 35 TDI in the Audi A4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The "35 TDI" badge is simply Audi's WLTP naming convention introduced around 2020 to denote the 150hp 2.0 TDI engine (typically DETA or EA288 Evo codes). Mechanically, it is the same 2.0L diesel architecture as the older CNHA, just with updated emissions mapping and mild-hybrid alternator integration on some late B9 models. 2.0 TDI: Pre-2020 naming (140hp, 150hp, 170hp, 190hp). 35 TDI: Post-2020 WLTP naming (specifically 150hp). 40 TDI: Post-2020 WLTP naming (specifically 190hp).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A4 B8 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For B8 models (2008-2015) valued between £4,000 and £12,000, a rebuilt engine at £3,200-£5,000 can represent a significant portion of the car's value. If your B8 is a high-spec S line or Quattro in excellent cosmetic condition, replacement is viable. For base SE models under £5,000, evaluate the scrap value first. Sub-£5,000 B8: Used engine or scrap is usually the financial reality. £6,000-£12,000 B8: Reconditioned engine is a safe, value-retaining investment. Always check for timing chain and turbo health before committing.

mainEntity.name: Are EA288 (B9) engines more reliable than EA189 (B8) engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the EA288 family (CNHA, DEUA) introduced in the B9 generation is generally more robust than the EA189. The EA288 moved the timing chain to the front of the engine (easier maintenance) and improved the high-pressure fuel pump. However, the EA288 is more sensitive to AdBlue system failures and urban DPF clogging. EA189: Prone to post-software-fix EGR/DPF soot issues. EA288: Prone to AdBlue crystallisation and NOx sensor faults. Both benefit from regular motorway driving to clear emissions systems.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete engine swap on an Audi A4 typically takes 1.5 to 2.5 days for a supply-and-fit service. The B9 generation requires additional time for AdBlue system priming, ECU component protection removal, and online immobiliser coding via ODIS (Audi's diagnostic system). Engine removal and installation: 10-14 hours. ECU coding and AdBlue calibration: 2-4 hours. Road testing and DPF regeneration cycle: 2-3 hours.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement Audi A4 2.0 TDI engine affect my car's MOT?

acceptedAnswer.text: A properly installed, correct-code replacement engine will not negatively affect your MOT, provided the emissions hardware (DPF, EGR, AdBlue) is fully intact and functional. In fact, replacing a worn engine blowing blue smoke or suffering from severe compression loss is often the only way to pass an emissions MOT on a high-mileage diesel. Engine number changes must be documented on the V5C logbook. Emissions tampering (DPF deletes) will result in an immediate MOT failure. Rebuilt engines include fresh injector seals to prevent "Black Death" leaks.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.0 TDI badge has been the core commercial and fleet diesel option in the A4 range since the B8 generation, evolving through the EA189 and EA288 engine families before adopting the 35 TDI WLTP naming convention in 2020.

milestones.description: B8 generation launches with EA189 2.0 TDI (140hp/170hp), CAGA/CFFB/CAHA engine codes, transitioning to common rail injection
B8 facelift refines EA189 engine mapping and emissions hardware for Euro 5 compliance
B9 generation debuts with EA288 2.0 TDI (150hp/190hp), CNHA/DEUA engine codes, featuring improved efficiency and AdBlue integration
B9 facelift introduces updated EA288 Evo variants for stricter Euro 6d-TEMP emissions standards
WLTP naming convention adopted; 150hp variants officially badged as 35 TDI (DETA/EA288 Evo), while 190hp variants become 40 TDI

commonProblems.h2: Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI is a highly capable executive diesel, but high-mileage examples frequently face emissions system failures, EGR blockages, and AdBlue faults. The CAGA/CFFB (EA189) and CNHA/DETA (EA288) codes dominate replacement demand for this variant, particularly on B8 and early B9 generation cars with 100k+ miles. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR & DPF Blockage - Why the Audi A4 2.0 TDI EA189 Chokes Post-Software Update
problems.rootCause: The mandatory Dieselgate emissions software fix altered injection timing and EGR flow rates, causing excessive soot buildup that rapidly clogs the EGR valve and DPF, eventually triggering limp mode and MOT emissions failures.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Off-car or on-car chemical flush of soot deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; blockage usually returns within 10k-20k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New OEM EGR cooler/valve and replacement DPF unit
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine internals are healthy and car is used for motorway miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded EGR flow paths, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best when DPF failure caused secondary turbo contamination or oil dilution

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Audi A4 B8 2.0 TDI (2008-2015) is currently worth £4,000-£12,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader UK 2025 data]. - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Many early B8 examples sit at the £4k-£6k watch threshold; evaluate scrap value before committing to a £3,800+ rebuilt engine.
problems.recommendation: If the DPF is physically melted or the turbo is contaminated with soot, cleaning is a waste of money. A rebuilt engine with a fresh emissions pathway is the only reliable long-term fix, but only if the host vehicle's chassis and interior condition justify the £3,000+ investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CAGA/CFFB Audi A4 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue & NOx Sensor Failure - Why the Audi A4 35 TDI EA288 Refuses to Start
problems.affectedModels: Audi A4 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI (CNHA, DEUA, DETA, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue injector crystallises with urea deposits, or the NOx sensors fail electronically, causing the ECU to initiate a strict countdown to a non-start condition to comply with Euro 6 emissions regulations.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty NOx sensor or crystallised injector
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the main AdBlue pump and tank are unaffected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace entire integrated tank, pump, and level sensor
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary when internal pump failure triggers ECU lockouts

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit with updated ECU mapping, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if AdBlue fluid leaked into the engine bay and destroyed electronics

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Audi A4 B9 35 TDI / 2.0 TDI (2015-present) is valued £8,000-£22,000 [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader UK 2025 data]. This places the B9 firmly in the "Safe" replacement category. A £2,800-£4,500 rebuilt engine represents a sensible percentage of the vehicle's value, ensuring the car remains reliable and MOT-compliant for years to come.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue faults rarely require a full engine replacement unless catastrophic collateral damage has occurred. Usually, a specialist AdBlue system overhaul (£800-£1,500) resolves the non-start issue. However, if the EA288 engine has also suffered timing chain stretch or EGR cooler internal leaks simultaneously, a rebuilt engine becomes the most cost-effective route to restore the vehicle.
